name: Mythic Hekatonkheires
body:
Mythic Hekatonkheires
CR 29/MR 10

This behemoth is a towering humanoid with fifty heads and twice as many hands, each wielding a different weapon.

XP 6,560,000
CE Colossal outsider (chaotic, evil, extraplanar, mythic)
Init +6; Senses all-around vision, darkvision 120 ft., true seeing; Perception +35; Aura planar guardian (60 ft.)

DEFENSE

AC 52, touch 12, flat-footed 50 (+8 deflection, +2 Dex, +40 natural, -8 size)
hp 664 (24d10+532); regeneration 10 (epic)
Fort +32, Ref +12, Will +18
Defensive Abilities fortification (50%), immortal vitality, unstoppable; DR 20/epic and lawful; Immune aging, blindness, dazzled, deafness, death effects, disease, mind-affecting effects; SR 45

OFFENSE

Speed 60 ft.; air walk
Melee +5 weapon +45/+45/+40/+35/+30 (6d6+38/19-20/x3 plus hundred-handed whirlwind) or slam +40 (4d8+33 plus stun)
Ranged rock +23/+18/+13/+8 (4d8+38/18-20)
Space 30 ft.; Reach 30 ft.
Special Attacks feral savagery (full attack), mythic spell-like abilities, rain of thunderstones, rock throwing (200 ft.), pounce, powerful blows, stunning slam, surge (1d12, 10/day)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 20th; concentration +27)

Constant—air walk, spell turning, true seeing
At will—bestow curse (DC 21), break enchantment, chain lightning (DC 23), greater dispel magic, find the path, sending
3/day—greater scrying (DC 24), quickened heal, mass suggestion (DC 23)
1/day—dominate monster (DC 26), greater spell immunity, imprisonment (DC 26), storm of vengeance (DC 26)

STATISTICS

Str 54, Dex 15, Con 47, Int 22, Wis 19, Cha 24
Base Atk +24; CMB +54; CMD 74
Feats Combat Expertise, Combat Reflexes, Critical Focus, Deflect Arrows MF, Greater Vital Strike, Improved Critical (hundred-handed whirlwind), Improved Initiative, Improved Vital Strike, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack MF, Quicken Spell-like Ability (heal), Staggering Critical, Vital Strike, Weapon Focus (hundred-handed strike)
Skills Acrobatics +29 (+41 when jumping), Bluff +34, Climb +46, Craft (any) +33, Diplomacy +31, Escape Artist +29, Intimidate +34, Knowledge (history) +30, Knowledge (planes) +33, Perception +31, Sense Motive +31, Survival +28
Languages Abyssal, Celestial, Common; telepathy 300 ft.
SQ half-hundred-headed, hands of war, planar leap, planar guardian

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Half-Hundred-Headed (Ex)

A hekatonkheires’ multitude of heads look every direction at once and keep watch. The titan cannot be blinded, dazzled, or deafened, and when it makes Perception checks it can roll twice and take the better result.

Hands of War (Su)

Any weapon a hekatonkheires wields gains a +5 enhancement bonus while the titan holds it. A hekatonkheires’s attacks are treated as epic, chaotic, and evil for the purposes of overcoming damage reduction. In addition, a hekatonkheires’s multitude of arms allows it to effectively block attacks, granting it a +8 deflection bonus to its AC. The hekatonkheires also is treated as having Improved Unarmed Strike for the purpose of feat prerequisites and treats its hundred-handed whirlwind as a single weapon for the purpose of feats.

Hundred-Handed Whirlwind (Ex)

A hekatonkheires carries several dozen weapons of various types in its hundred hands, but when it attacks in melee, you don’t have to resolve each of these as a separate attack. Instead, when the titan attacks with its weapons, it rolls its attacks normally (either one attack for a standard action, or four as a full-round action) and hits every creature in its reach each time an attack roll exceeds that creature’s AC. If any such attack roll results in a possible critical hit, the critical is applied to one creature of the hekatonkheires’s choosing. The hekatonkheires can choose to deal bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage as a free action on each separate hit.

Immortal Vitality (Ex)

A mythic hekatonkheires cannot be magically aged and cannot die of old age. Any ability damage or drain (including temporary penalties to ability scores, such as those from fatigue, exhaustion, or ray of enfeeblement) or negative levels it would gain are halved. It also can expend one use of mythic power as an immediate action to ignore all ability damage or drain or negative levels from a single effect.

Mythic Spell-Like Abilities (Su)

Three times per day, a mythic hekatonkheires may use the mythic spell version of any of its corresponding spell-like abilities. She must expend the same amount of mythic power that would normally be required to cast a mythic spell, treating her mythic rank as her mythic tier for the purpose of qualifying to use augmented versions of mythic spells.

Planar Guardian (Su)

The three mythic hekatonkheires are the wardens of Tartarus and guardians of planar portals. Conjuration (teleportation) effects do not function within 60 feet unless the hekatonkheires wishes, nor does any form of plane travel, or movement between coterminous planes like the Ethereal and Plane of Shadow. Incorporeal creatures within 60 feet of the hekatonkheires cannot move through solid objects or creatures, and the hekatonkheires’ attacks and special abilities affect incorporeal creatures as if they were not incorporeal. If a creature within 60 feet of the hekatonkheires attempts to use a conjuration (teleportation) effect, the titan can expend one use of its mythic power to cast imprisonment on that creature as an immediate action.

Planar Leap (Su)

A hekatonkheires traverses the planes by physically smashing through planar boundaries and crashing devastatingly into the target plane itself. Once per year as a full-round action, a hekatonkheires can, as part of a jump, plane shift to any other plane (as per the spell of the same name). It can only bring itself and its gear when it travels in this manner. When the hekatonkheires reaches its destination plane, it falls from the sky and crashes to the ground, creating a devastating explosion of thunder and fire. Any creature within 300 feet of the point where the hekatonkheires lands (including the titan itself) takes 20d6 points of bludgeoning damage and 20d6 points of sonic damage (DC 40 Reflex half). The save DC is Constitution-based.

Rain of Thunderstones (Su)

As a full-round action, a mythic hekatonkheires can hurl a rain of massive boulders infused with the power of lightning and thunder in four 200-foot lines, dealing 6d6 points each of bludgeoning, electricity, and sonic damage (DC 40 Reflex half). Creatures that fail their saving throw must succeed on a DC 40 Fortitude save or be blinded for 1 round and deafened for 1 minute.

Stunning Slam (Ex)

As a standard action, a hekatonkheires may forgo any weapon attacks to make a single slam attack against all creatures in a 10-foot cube, making a single attack roll and comparing it to the AC of each creature. If it hits, the target takes damage and must succeed at a DC 44 Fortitude save to avoid being stunned for 1d6 rounds. The save DC is Strength-based.

Unstoppable (Ex)

A mythic hekatonkheires can expend one use of mythic power as a free action to end any of the following conditions affecting it: bleed, blind, confused, cowering, dazed, dazzled, deafened, entangled, exhausted, fascinated, fatigued, frightened, nauseated, panicked, paralyzed, shaken, sickened, staggered, or stunned. Other effects remain, even if they came from the same effect that caused the chosen condition. It can use this ability at the start of its turn even if it would normally be unable to take actions.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary
Treasure triple (50-100 various weapons, other treasure)

These elder titans were created by the first gods to awaken, and they made only only three monstrous brothers: Gyes, Cottus, and Briareus. These horrifying abominations were birthed to guard the gates of the Tarterian Abyss but were shunned by the gods immediately upon their creation.

Perhaps the the most powerful and devastating race of titans in existence, when their titanic kin—envious of the gods’ divine strength—rebelled against these new deities, the hekatonkheires were among the first to pick up arms, weary of the scorn their own creators felt for them. The betrayal of the Elysian titans led to the hekatonkheires’ swift capture by the gods, who found the hekatonkheires’ power to be so immense that they were not banished to the Abyss with their Thanatotic brethren. Instead, the gods cast the hekatonkheires into the furthest reaches of the multiverse they could find. There, the hekatonkheires drifted in expanses of nothingness for unknown eons, and the madness wrought upon them by isolation destroyed their memories. Yet from their madness these shattered monstrosities spawned lesser titanic progeny to replace them in their pursuit to destroy, and some of these monstrous offspring discovered ways to break through planar boundaries and wander the multiverse freely.
